anzsic_codes.name: Wine and Other Alcoholic Beverage Manufacturing

merger_description:
Sazerac Company, Inc. (together with its corporate group, **Sazerac**) proposes to acquire 100% of the shares of Aurous Topco Limited, and its subsidiaries, relevantly including Au Vodka Ltd (together, **Au Vodka**) (the **Acquisition**).

Sazerac is an American alcoholic beverage company specialising in spirits. It owns over 525 brands and 18 distilling and bottling facilities worldwide. Sazerac manufactures a range of products including bourbon, American whiskey, vodka, rum and tequila, pre-mixed cocktails and cordials. It also manufactures complementary products such as bitters and non-alcoholic products. In addition to manufacturing, Sazerac distributes its own and some (limited) third parties' products, and also operates spirit distilleries. Sazerac distributes its products globally through both direct sales and distribution channels. In Australia, Sazerac’s sales are made through an Australian subsidiary which imports and supplies the products at wholesale prices to distributors. Sazerac has no manufacturing facilities in Australia.

Au Vodka is a UK-based alcoholic beverage brand that supplies vodka products (including both spirits and ready-to-drink products) globally across approximately 50 countries. Au Vodka does not have any employees or a physical presence in Australia; its products are imported and distributed in Australia through a third-party distributor.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. the parties’ combined share in the wholesale supply of
vodka and RTDs in Australia is low and the increment arising
from the Acquisition would be small
• b. there are alternative wholesale suppliers of vodka and RTDs
in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
